title: How much RAM Mac Mini M6 for AI Research Trading System?
author: IAMBLVNCO
selftext:
I was wondering if 24GB RAM is enough to run a Mac Mini in the background as a full time Research Trading System, who later will be upgraded to a Trading Bot. 

I have a fully spect out Macbook Pro M1 for daily use, so the Mac Mini is purely for running the whole system. I’m using Claude Code Opus 5 High to run it and ChatGPT Sol 5.6 Ultra to audit the system.

comments.author: fomoz
comments.body:
You mean to run the app, not the inference, right? Should be enough assuming it's just a few bots. If you want to have many users, etc., you're better off getting a VPS.

I'd be more concerned with the internet or electricity going down at your house.

replies.author: IAMBLVNCO
replies.body: I’m building it purely for myself as a Quant system.

replies.author: fomoz
replies.body: I think it's enough, but you can also run something like Netdata if you want to be sure about system usage and headroom. If it's maxing out the Mac Mini you might have some arch issues/memory leak/inefficient DB and so on.

replies.author: IAMBLVNCO
replies.body:
Alright. Thanks!  
Regarding electricity/internet bill, I’m living in Bangkok so prices are crazy cheap here compared to Western standards. Also the Mac Mini doesn’t draw much power at all.

replies.author: fomoz
replies.body: I meant if you have an outage for electricity or Internet, compared to using a VPS in a data center that's probably more reliable (or two VPS with load balancing and so on).

replies.author: IAMBLVNCO
replies.body: Yeah true. Although can use a KVM and auto login and auto boothing after power outage.

comments.author: Cancington42
comments.body:
You might be better off building a pc and running linux. I built a quant machine and use it for RL, ML, and algo work. I only use the system for database management, data curation, rnd and dev work. I run my strategies on a vps, and a uconsole. 

You’ll also want tons of storage and multiple drives for workflows and backups. I think I have about 80tb between 8 drives, ssd, nvme, hdd, and one external drive to back up the whold system, all with btrfs volumes and zstd 3-9 depending on the drive. That way 80tb logistical can actually hold 10-15x all the financial data that you’ll end up transforming, and all the data for your experiments. 

Building and customizing your own quant system is the right way to go, then you can have full system admin. I use NixOS.

Backup everything in triplicate.

Enjoy!

replies.author: IAMBLVNCO
replies.body: Well I’m still a beginner but I’m a fast learner. Thanks for your insights! Some is a bit gibberish to me, but hopefully I’ll understand it all pretty fast haha.

replies.author: IAMBLVNCO
replies.body:
Well so, I’m building it mainly to backtest and find the right strategy for me to use with prop firms. I have income from other jobs so I have time enough to build something that works for me to trading and hopefully later to automate it trading. I don’t need to get rich from it. Just as a bonus.

That said, I’m running it now with an MCP to Tradingview. Checking to buy data from Databento. It’s running mainly on Python. What do you suggest is the best way for me going forward?

replies.author: Cancington42
replies.body:
That’s exactly what I built mine for. I use python mostly, sometimes rust.

I built all the data pipelines, and the infrastructure for testing strategies. 

I’ve used massive.com for data, and hyperliquid has orderflow data s3 for cheap, websocket for free. 

Since you’re working with claude, I’d start with setting up and organizing your project properly, and setup a backup system. I lost 4tb of data because of a silly trailing slash. With your projects, set them up as repositories and use git to manage version control. A good place to start is getting some data, cleaning it, run it through quality control, then explore the data with your strategy with claude. Build modularly too.

replies.author: IAMBLVNCO
replies.body:
Alright great, thanks! What is the best/cheapest to get futures/forex data? Also what periods are you backtesting? I’ve build it with an OOS lock but Claude always seems to mess up on that part so I almost always have to wait for new data it says.  
I also have a context engine build into it now.

replies.author: Cancington42
replies.body:
Massive has forex and crypto tick data for 50$ I think 10 years crypto, and older for forex. It’s the cheapest tick data that I’ve found, and they have flat files. Download all the historical data, cancel your subscription and work with the data. 

I do combinatorial purged cross validation (cpcv) or walk forward with 1 year segments,  staggered by month. I also did regime classification as well and group by regime, with out of sample hold out as well. Once I generate a few seeds, I deploy it for paper trading on one of my servers and see how the strategy does with live data.

replies.author: IAMBLVNCO
replies.body: You’d say that is the best way of seeing the backtest results? Cuz the OOS lock I have now is not working for me. It’s also working on a 5 year period basis so I guess there is my bottleneck.

replies.author: Cancington42
replies.body:
You’re using claude to look at the data, then trade for you? That’s completely different than quant work. That’s giving an LLM an objective to trade. When building an algorithm for trading, the idea is finding an edge based on your strategy that’s repeatable on the evaluation data, then oos, then live. I’ve also worked with reinforcement learning by building a neural network through curriculum learning. Once you find a model that works out of sample, you deploy to paper trading live. 5 years is plenty enough data to use for regime cycles and backtesting, if you’re using the data for proper quantitative analysis. 

If your using claude or gpt, you could connect it to quantitative and qualitative data, fundamentals, and economic forecasting, and see if it could predict with high probability where the market might go, or use machine learning with a transformed feature enhanced dataset and see if any patterns emerge that produce alpha. Issue is, you’ll run into a lot of beta. Once you do that, you could paper trade with claude or GPT manually to measure your profit factor and sharpe.

comments.author: NefariousnessOpening
comments.body: using frontier models in the cloud is not going to use any VRAM for the models, the use cases you describe can work on practically any machine. disagree about building a PC. unified memory in apple silicon is more for less in the RL ML and algo domains and none of use are likely to have the spare millions of dollars necessary for the machines to do enterprise level ML Ops. a mac mini is cheap reliable, you can easily install linux, and you can contratry to popular belief install an eGPU if you ever outgrow the unified GPU. the actual results from apple silicon in my experience though are rather impressive and free up braincells from hardware work. MLX and some tuning will improve performance when running small model locally. you can increasse the amount of VRAM allocated with a simple one line command. you can also super easily bridge multiple silicon macbook with thunderbold, wifi, etc and have a cistributed computing cluster. its dead simple and just works. I run Kali Linux, Ubuntu, recently Omarchy on macbooks. its dope to be able to turn on a vm with a different OS without even need to dual boot and even share directories between them, persist volumes from the Linux OS when they turn off. you can have one machine with two simultanous OS, two differnent IP addresses even two separate network. I would strongly recommend exploring the other option available beyond Claude and ChatGPT. there are much much better ones available and for trading there are other LLM architectures that are better suited to some of the work. transformers do not have a sense of time which is a detriment given the amount of temporal data. there are other options like liquid neural net that do undesrtand temporal data

comments.author: ozgqr
comments.body: 24GB should be reasonable if Claude and ChatGPT are handling inference remotely and the Mini is mainly running orchestration, databases, and scheduled jobs. I’d budget memory per process, cap concurrent backtests, and watch swap before upgrading; local data pipelines and parallel experiments will usually matter more than the model UI. Marx could fit as one research component rather than another always-on worker.

comments.author: CODE_HEIST
comments.body:
24gb should be fine if the mini is orchestrating jobs and calling hosted models.



it gets tight with local inference, big tick datasets, or several parallel workers. imo keep research on the mini and eventual execution on a small vps with monitoring and restart controls. storage, backups, and reliable internet may become the bottleneck before cpu does.
